items.title: G20 Rio de Janeiro Summit (Brazil): Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty Launched
items.summary: The 19th G20 Summit convened in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, officially launching the 'Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty' and advancing the global governance reforms initiated during India's 2023 G20 Presidency.
items.crux: The summit focused on three core pillars: Social inclusion and the fight against hunger, energy transition and sustainable development, and reform of global governance institutions (UNSC, WTO, IMF).
takeaways: India, Brazil, and South Africa formed the G20 Troika, maintaining continuity on Global South priorities.
African Union (AU), inducted as a permanent member under India's G20 Presidency at New Delhi, participated in full capacity.
Endorsed progressive taxation on ultra-high-net-worth individuals and capital replenishment for Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs).

mcq.explanation: The flagship deliverable of Brazil's G20 presidency was the Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty, endorsed by over 80 countries.

items.title: 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia: Historic Expansion Welcomes 5 New Member States
items.summary: The 16th BRICS Summit convened in Kazan, Russia, under the theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', marking the first summit meeting since the formal expansion of BRICS to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates.
items.crux: Leaders adopted the comprehensive Kazan Declaration, reaffirming commitment to cross-border settlement in local currencies (BRICS Pay / BRICS Bridge) and reform of the Bretton Woods financial institutions and the UN Security Council.
takeaways: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held their first formal bilateral meeting in five years on the sidelines of the summit following the patrolling pact along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
BRICS represents over 45% of the world's population and roughly 35% of global GDP by Purchasing Power Parity (PPP).
Created a new category of 'BRICS Partner Countries' to engage non-member developing economies.

items.title: RBI Monetary Policy Stance & Liquidity Framework: Repo Rate Maintained at 6.50%
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) maintained the benchmark policy repo rate at 6.50% while shifting stance to 'Neutral' to support growth while ensuring inflation aligns durably with the 4% target.
items.crux: MPC retains repo rate at 6.50%, Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) at 6.25%, and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) at 6.75%, adopting a neutral stance to calibrate monetary conditions.
takeaways: MPC operates under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act 1934, comprising 6 members (3 from RBI, 3 external experts appointed by Central Government).
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) introduced in 2022 acts as the non-collateralized floor of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor.
Inflation projection pegged at 4.5% for FY25 with real GDP growth projected at 7.2%.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Repo: 6.50%, SDF: 6.25%, MSF: 6.75%, Bank Rate: 6.75%. Inflation target band: 4% ± 2%.

mcq.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) of the RBI is correct?
options: It requires the RBI to provide government securities as collateral to absorbing banks.
It allows the RBI to absorb excess liquidity from commercial banks without providing collateral.
It operates at a rate 25 basis points higher than the Policy Repo Rate.
It was recommended by the Chakravarty Committee in 1985.
mcq.explanation: SDF was introduced under Section 17 of the RBI Act in 2022 to absorb liquidity without collateral, positioned 25 bps below the Repo Rate.

items.title: Classical Language Status Conferred on 5 New Indian Languages
items.summary: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi conferred the prestigious status of 'Classical Language' on five languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali, expanding the total count of Classical Languages in India from 6 to 11.
items.crux: Criteria for Classical Language status include high antiquity of early texts over 1,500–2,000 years, a body of ancient literature considered valuable heritage, and original literary tradition.
takeaways: Previously 6 Classical Languages: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu (2008), Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014).
Status enables two major annual international awards for scholars, dedicated university chairs, and Centers of Excellence for studies.
Pali and Prakrit are foundational to early Buddhist canonical texts (Tripitaka) and Jain Agamas respectively.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total Classical Languages now: 11 (Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali).

mcq.question: With the recent notification in October 2024 adding Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali, how many languages in India now enjoy 'Classical Language' status?
mcq.explanation: With the addition of 5 new languages to the existing 6 (Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia), the total count of Classical Languages in India reached 11.

items.title: 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad Budapest: Historic Double Gold in Open and Women's Sections
items.summary: India achieved an unprecedented double gold medal triumph at the 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Budapest, Hungary, winning both the Open section (Hamilton-Russell Cup) and the Women's section (Vera Menchik Cup).
items.crux: India became only the third country in chess history (after Soviet Union and China) to win both titles at the same Olympiad, with D Gukesh, Arjun Erigaisi, Divya Deshmukh, and Vantika Agrawal also winning individual board gold medals.
takeaways: Open Team: D Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa R, Arjun Erigaisi, Vidit Gujrathi, and Pentala Harikrishna.
Women's Team: Harika Dronavalli, Vaishali Rameshbabu, Divya Deshmukh, Vantika Agrawal, and Tania Sachdev.
Gukesh posted a staggering 27-point tournament performance rating above 3050, winning 9 out of 10 games.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 45th edition; Double Gold; Open trophy: Hamilton-Russell Cup; Women's trophy: Vera Menchik Cup.

mcq.question: At the 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Budapest 2024, the Indian Men's team lifted which historic championship trophy?
options: Vera Menchik Cup
Hamilton-Russell Cup
Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy
Fischer Memorial Shield
mcq.explanation: The Hamilton-Russell Cup is awarded to the winners of the Open section, while the Vera Menchik Cup is awarded to the Women's section.

items.title: Quad Leaders' Summit in Wilmington: Quad Cancer Moonshot & MAITRI Initiative Launched

items.crux: Leaders unveiled the 'Quad Cancer Moonshot' to combat cervical cancer across the Indo-Pacific and the Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific (MAITRI) to empower regional coast guards.

items.title: Paris 2024 Paralympics: India's Record 29 Medals & Sumit Antil Back-to-Back Gold
items.summary: India delivered its best-ever performance in Paralympic history at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, winning 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze) and finishing 18th in the overall medal table.
items.crux: Sumit Antil became the first Indian man to defend a Paralympic title with Gold in Javelin (F64, 70.59m Games Record), while Navdeep Singh secured Gold in Javelin (F41), and Avani Lekhara defended her 10m Air Rifle Gold.

items.title: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024: India's Largest-Ever Multilateral Air Force Combat Drill
items.summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) conducted 'Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024', the largest multilateral air combat exercise ever hosted on Indian soil, involving air forces from over 30 countries in two phases across Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan.
items.crux: Phase 1 was conducted at Sulur Air Force Station (Tamil Nadu) featuring Germany, France, Spain, and the UK, while Phase 2 took place at Jodhpur (Rajasthan) with participation from the US, Australia, Greece, UAE, and Singapore.
takeaways: Showcased indigenous aviation platforms including LCA Tejas Mk1, Light Combat Helicopter (Prachand), and ALH Dhruv.

Strengthens interoperability, combat tactics, and strategic defence partnerships with Quad, European, and Middle Eastern allies.

Hindon Air Force Station, Uttar Pradesh
mcq.explanation: Phase 1 of Tarang Shakti was held at Sulur Air Force Station in Tamil Nadu, followed by Phase 2 at Jodhpur Air Force Station in Rajasthan.

items.title: Colombo Security Conclave (CSC): Founding Charter Signed for Maritime Security
items.summary: India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Mauritius formally signed the founding Charter and Memorandum of Understanding establishing the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) as a institutionalized regional security grouping in the Indian Ocean.

items.title: INS Arighaat Commissioned: India's Second SSBN Nuclear Ballistic Submarine
items.summary: India commissioned its second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), INS Arighaat (S3), into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, cementing India's survivable nuclear triad.
items.crux: INS Arighaat joins lead vessel INS Arihant in the Strategic Forces Command (SFC), armed with K-15 Sagarika (750 km range) and K-4 (3,500 km range) submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBMs).

items.title: Digital Rupee (CBDC) Expansion: Offline Capability & Programmable Targeted Use-Cases
items.summary: The RBI introduced offline functionality and programmability for the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e-Rupee) in both retail (CBDC-R) and wholesale (CBDC-W) segments.
items.crux: Programmability enables targeted purpose-bound disbursements such as agricultural carbon credits or school subsidies, while offline capability enables transactions in remote low-connectivity regions.
takeaways: CBDC is a sovereign legal tender issued by the central bank in digital form, appearing as a direct liability on RBI's balance sheet.
Operates via a two-tier model where RBI issues tokens and commercial banks distribute them to retail wallets.
Interoperability with UPI QR codes allows merchants to accept e-Rupee using their existing UPI scan infrastructure.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 (amended by Finance Act 2022, Sec 2)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: CBDC is fungible 1:1 with fiat currency; does not earn interest; legal tender.

Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
mcq.explanation: CBDC is a direct sovereign liability of the RBI (not commercial banks) and is non-interest bearing to avoid disintermediation of bank deposits.

items.title: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) Completes 10 Years: 53+ Crore Accounts & ₹2.3 Lakh Crore Deposits
items.summary: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on August 28, 2014, completed a decade of operation, achieving over 53 crore bank accounts with cumulative deposits exceeding ₹2.3 lakh crore.
items.crux: Over 55% of PMJDY account holders are women and nearly 67% of accounts are in rural and semi-urban areas, serving as the foundation of the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) Trinity.
takeaways: Zero minimum balance requirement with a free RuPay debit card carrying ₹2 lakh accidental insurance cover.
Overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000 provided to eligible account holders.
Serves as the pipeline for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) across PM-KISAN, PAHAL, and scholarship welfare programs.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Launched: 28 August 2014. Motto: 'Mera Khata Bhagya Vidhata'. RuPay accidental cover: ₹2 Lakh.

mcq.question: What is the maximum overdraft (OD) facility available under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) per eligible household?
mcq.explanation: The overdraft limit under PMJDY was doubled from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, with no conditions asked for OD up to ₹2,000.

items.title: Unified Lending Interface (ULI): RBI Launches Frictionless Digital Credit Architecture
items.summary: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das announced the nationwide rollout of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI), a technology platform designed to enable seamless, consent-based flow of digital financial and land record data to credit institutions.
items.crux: Just as UPI transformed retail payments, ULI is designed to revolutionize lending by reducing loan appraisal turnaround times from weeks to minutes, especially for small farmers and MSMEs.
takeaways: ULI integrates data silos including state land records, satellite imagery, milk pouring data from dairy cooperatives, and Aadhaar e-KYC.
Developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH), a wholly-owned subsidiary of RBI.
Employs a 'plug-and-play' open architecture with standardized APIs, reducing documentation burden for borrower.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: ULI acronym: Unified Lending Interface; focus: rural, agriculture, and MSME credit.

mcq.question: The newly launched Unified Lending Interface (ULI) by RBI is primarily aimed at:
options: Replacing the RTGS interbank transfer network.
Enabling frictionless, consent-based credit appraisal using digitized land and financial records.
Facilitating cross-border currency trading for retail investors.
Regulating non-performing assets of urban cooperative banks.
mcq.explanation: ULI enables consent-based digital data sharing (land records, satellite data, dairy pouring data) to facilitate rapid, paperless credit evaluation.

items.title: 3rd Voice of Global South Summit (VOGSS): India Champions Developing World Priorities
items.summary: India hosted the 3rd Voice of Global South Summit virtually under the theme 'An Empowered Global South for a Sustainable Future', bringing together leaders from over 120 developing nations across Asia, Africa, and Latin America.
items.crux: Prime Minister Modi proposed a comprehensive 'Global South Development Compact' focused on trade, technology sharing, concessional finance, and human resource capacity building without imposing debt burdens.
takeaways: India operationalized the DAKSHIN (Development and Knowledge Sharing Initiative) Global South Center of Excellence.
Promotes the 'Arogya Maitri' project supplying life-saving medical supplies to crisis-hit developing nations.
Reiterates demand for reform of the UN Security Council and international financial institutions (IMF/World Bank).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Theme: 'An Empowered Global South for a Sustainable Future'; Center of Excellence: DAKSHIN; Health initiative: Arogya Maitri.

mcq.question: Which Center of Excellence was established by India to coordinate knowledge-sharing and sustainable development solutions with developing countries?
options: SAMARTH
DAKSHIN
SANKALP
MAITRI
mcq.explanation: DAKSHIN (Development and Knowledge Sharing Initiative) was established by India as a specialized Center of Excellence for Global South nations.

items.title: India Adds 3 New Ramsar Sites: Total Network Reaches 85 Wetlands of Global Importance
items.summary: On the eve of Independence Day, India designated three new wetlands under the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands—Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary and Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu, and Tawa Reservoir in Madhya Pradesh—expanding India's Ramsar network to 85 sites.
items.crux: India has the second largest network of Ramsar sites in Asia after China, with Tamil Nadu hosting the highest number of Ramsar sites in India (18 sites), followed by Uttar Pradesh (10 sites).
takeaways: Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary (Tiruppur, TN): 83rd site, an ancient large irrigation tank home to migratory waterbirds on the Central Asian Flyway.
Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary (Villupuram, TN): 84th site, second largest brackish water lake in South India after Pulicat Lake.
Tawa Reservoir (Hoshangabad, MP): 85th site, situated inside Satpura Tiger Reserve at the confluence of Tawa and Denwa rivers.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) & Ramsar Secretariat
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ramsar Convention 1971 & Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total Ramsar sites: 85; State with most sites: Tamil Nadu (18); World Wetlands Day: 2 February.

mcq.question: Which Indian State currently possesses the highest number of Ramsar Sites (18 wetlands of international importance) in India?
options: Uttar Pradesh
Kerala
Tamil Nadu
Madhya Pradesh
mcq.explanation: Tamil Nadu leads India with 18 Ramsar sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10 sites.

items.title: Paris 2024 Olympics: Manu Bhaker Historic Double Bronze in Shooting
items.summary: Manu Bhaker created history at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, becoming the first athlete in independent India's history to win two Olympic medals in a single edition of the Games.
items.crux: Bhaker won Bronze in the Women's 10m Air Pistol individual event and a second Bronze in the 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team event alongside Sarabjot Singh.
takeaways: India concluded Paris 2024 with 6 medals: 1 Silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 Bronze (Manu Bhaker x2, Swapnil Kusale, Men's Hockey, Aman Sehrawat).
Swapnil Kusale won India's first-ever Olympic medal (Bronze) in the Men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions event.
Aman Sehrawat (57kg Freestyle wrestling) became India's youngest individual Olympic medalist at age 21.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) & Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Manu Bhaker: 2 medals in single Olympics; Total Paris medals: 6 (1 Silver, 5 Bronze).

mcq.question: Who became the first athlete in independent India's history to win two medals in a single edition of the Olympic Games at Paris 2024?
options: PV Sindhu
Manu Bhaker
Neeraj Chopra
Mirabai Chanu
mcq.explanation: Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in Paris 2024 (10m Air Pistol individual and 10m Air Pistol mixed team).

items.title: Neeraj Chopra Wins Javelin Silver at Paris 2024 Olympics (89.45m Throw)
items.summary: Reigning Olympic and World Champion Neeraj Chopra won the Silver medal in the Men's Javelin Throw at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games with a season-best throw of 89.45 meters at the Stade de France.
items.crux: Chopra became the first Indian track-and-field athlete in post-independence history to win back-to-back Olympic medals (Gold at Tokyo 2020, Silver at Paris 2024).
takeaways: Gold was won by Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem with a monstrous Olympic Record throw of 92.97 meters.
Chopra became the fourth Indian athlete in post-independence history to win multiple individual Olympic medals after Norman Pritchard, Sushil Kumar, PV Sindhu, and Manu Bhaker.
Followed by his 2023 World Athletics Championship Gold in Budapest (88.17m).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Silver medal; Throw: 89.45 meters; Gold: Arshad Nadeem (92.97m OR).

mcq.question: Neeraj Chopra secured the Silver medal in the Men's Javelin Throw final at the Paris 2024 Olympics with a throw of:
options: 87.58 meters
88.17 meters
89.45 meters
90.18 meters
mcq.explanation: Neeraj Chopra produced a throw of 89.45 meters on his second attempt to win the Olympic Silver medal.

items.title: SC/ST Sub-Classification Allowed: 7-Judge Constitution Bench Verdict (Davinder Singh Case)
items.summary: A landmark 7-judge Constitution Bench held by a 6:1 majority that State legislatures are constitutionally empowered to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to grant preferential reservation to more backward groups.
items.crux: The judgment overruled the 2004 5-judge bench decision in E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh, holding that SCs do not form an indivisible, homogenous class.
takeaways: Sub-classification must be based on verifiable empirical data demonstrating inadequate representation, not political expediency.
States cannot reserve 100% of seats for any sub-group, nor can they exclude any caste from the Presidential list under Article 341 entirely.
Four of the six majority judges observed that the 'Creamy Layer' principle should also apply to SCs and STs.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Articles 14, 15, 16(4), 341, and 342 of Constitution of India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Case: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024); Majority: 6:1 (Dissent: Justice Bela M. Trivedi).

mcq.question: Which earlier landmark judgment was overruled by the 7-judge Constitution Bench regarding sub-classification of Scheduled Castes in 2024?
options: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2004)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
mcq.explanation: The 7-judge bench overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004), which had previously held that SCs constitute a homogenous monolith that cannot be sub-divided.

items.title: Moidams of Ahom Dynasty in Assam Inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.summary: At the 46th session of the World Heritage Committee in New Delhi, the Charaideo Moidams (mound-burial system of the Ahom Dynasty) were inscribed onto the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming the first cultural site from Northeast India to gain this status.
items.crux: Known as the 'Pyramids of Assam', the Moidams represent the 600-year-old royal burial tradition and tai-ahom funerary architecture situated in Charaideo, the first capital of the Ahom kingdom founded by Chao Lung Siu-Ka-Pha in 1253 AD.
takeaways: India now has 43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (35 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed - Khangchendzonga).
Moidams feature a vaulted chamber (Chaw-Chali), earth mounds covered by grass, and octagonal boundary walls with a shrine on top (Chow-chali).
First World Heritage Committee session hosted by India took place in New Delhi in July 2024.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 43rd UNESCO World Heritage site in India; 1st cultural site from Northeast India; Built by Ahom kings (13th-18th century).

mcq.question: The Charaideo Moidams, recently inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site, belong to which historic ruling dynasty?
options: Pala Dynasty
Koch Dynasty
Ahom Dynasty
Kamata Dynasty
mcq.explanation: Moidams are the sacred royal burial mounds of the Ahom kings and queens in Charaideo, Assam, who ruled the Brahmaputra valley for over 600 years.

items.title: Moidams of Assam Inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.summary: The 'Moidams—the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty' in Charaideo, Assam, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 46th World Heritage Committee session in New Delhi, becoming India's 43rd World Heritage site.
items.crux: Charaideo Moidams represents the first cultural World Heritage site from Northeast India, showcasing the 600-year-old vaulted earthen burial architecture of Tai-Ahom royals compared to the Egyptian pyramids.
takeaways: Charaideo was the first capital established by Chaolung Sukaphaa, founder of the Ahom dynasty, in 1253 CE.
A Moidam consists of a domical mound housing a vaulted brick chamber (chow-chali), covered with earth and a hemispherical earthen superstructure.
India now has 43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (35 Cultural, 7 Natural, and 1 Mixed - Khangchendzonga).

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 43rd site in India; 1st cultural site in NE India; Ahom dynasty (1228-1826 CE); Founder: Chaolung Sukaphaa.

mcq.question: Which royal dynasty built the pyramidal earthen burial mound system known as 'Moidams' in Charaideo, Assam?
options: Kamata Dynasty
Ahom Dynasty
Koch Dynasty
Varman Dynasty
mcq.explanation: The Moidams are the sacred vaulted mound-burial tumuli of royalty belonging to the Tai-Ahom dynasty of Assam.

items.title: Fiscal Deficit Consolidation & New Tax Regime (Sec 115BAC) Structural Reforms
items.summary: Union Budget 2024-25 targeted a fiscal deficit of 4.9% of GDP, consolidating on track to achieve below 4.5% by FY26, alongside structural tax revisions in the default New Personal Income Tax Regime.
items.crux: Standard deduction under the New Tax Regime increased to ₹75,000 for salaried employees, tax slabs revised, and Capex outlay sustained at a record ₹11.11 lakh crore (3.4% of GDP).
takeaways: Fiscal Deficit glide path anchored under Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act 2003 principles.
Over two-thirds of personal income tax filers transitioned to the simplified New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC).
Record ₹11.11 lakh crore central capital expenditure aimed at multiplier effects on roads, railways, and urban infrastructure.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Finance & Department of Revenue
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Fiscal Deficit FY25 target: 4.9%; FY26 target: below 4.5%; Standard Deduction: ₹75,000; Capex: ₹11.11 Lakh Cr.

mcq.question: Under the Union Budget, what is the government's target for fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP for financial year 2024-25?
mcq.explanation: The revised Union Budget estimated the fiscal deficit for FY 2024-25 at 4.9% of GDP, continuing the fiscal consolidation glide path to reach below 4.5% by FY26.

items.title: UPI Goes Global: Cross-Border Linkages Live in UAE, France, Singapore, Mauritius & Sri Lanka
items.summary: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) expanded Unified Payments Interface (UPI) acceptance across France (Eiffel Tower merchant payments), UAE (interlinked with AANI), Singapore (PayNow-UPI link), Mauritius, and Sri Lanka.
items.crux: Cross-border linkage enables Indian travelers and the diaspora to make instant merchant payments and inward remittances directly from rupee bank accounts via QR codes.
takeaways: Operated by NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of NPCI incorporated in 2020.
Real-time linkage with Singapore's PayNow was India's first cross-border real-time payment system linkage.
Promotes local currency settlement, reducing reliance on intermediary SWIFT correspondent banking fees.

prelims_pointers.location: France, UAE, Singapore, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Nepal
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: NPCI is an initiative of RBI and IBA under PSS Act 2007; Section 8 not-for-profit company.

mcq.question: Which subsidiary of NPCI is dedicated to deploying UPI and RuPay payment architectures internationally?
options: NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited (NBBL)
NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL)
Digital India Payments Corporation
RBI Payments Overseas Ltd
mcq.explanation: NIPL was established in April 2020 as the international arm of NPCI to drive cross-border deployment of UPI and RuPay.

items.title: 24th SCO Summit in Astana: Belarus Admitted as 10th Full Member State
items.summary: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State met in Astana, Kazakhstan, officially admitting the Republic of Belarus as the 10th full member state of the Eurasian security bloc.
items.crux: Leaders signed the Astana Declaration and approved the SCO Development Strategy until 2035, affirming cooperation against terrorism, separatism, and extremism ('three evils') and promoting settlement in national currencies.
takeaways: SCO now comprises 10 member states: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran, and Belarus.
External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar represented India, reiterating zero tolerance against cross-border terrorism and respect for sovereignty in connectivity.
China assumed the rotating SCO presidency for 2024–2025.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 10th member: Belarus (joined 2024); 9th member was Iran (joined 2023); RATS HQ: Tashkent, Uzbekistan; SCO Sec: Beijing.

mcq.question: Which nation was formally inducted as the 10th full member state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at the 2024 Astana Summit?
options: Armenia
Belarus
Mongolia
Azerbaijan
mcq.explanation: Belarus became the 10th full member of the SCO at the Astana Summit in July 2024.

items.title: New Criminal Laws Enacted: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, BNSS & BSA Come into Effect
items.summary: Three new criminal laws—Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS 2023), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS 2023), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA 2023)—formally came into force across India, replacing the Indian Penal Code 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, and Indian Evidence Act 1872.
items.crux: The laws introduce community service as a penal punishment, mandatory videography of search and seizure, electronic Zero FIR, and replace 'sedition' with acts endangering sovereignty and unity of India.
takeaways: BNS replaces Section 124A (Sedition) with Section 152 penalizing acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
Mandates forensic investigation for offences punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or more.
Introduces timelines for judgment delivery (within 30 days of argument conclusion, extendable to 45 days).

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: BNS Act 2023, BNSS Act 2023, BSA Act 2023
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: In force from: 1 July 2024. BNS has 358 sections (IPC had 511); BNSS has 531 sections; BSA has 170 sections.

mcq.question: Under the newly enforced Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which novel category of punishment was introduced into Indian criminal law?
options: Indefinite solitary confinement
Community service for minor offences
Exile to designated union territories
Civil death and total asset forfeiture
mcq.explanation: BNS introduces 'Community Service' as one of the six recognized forms of punishment for petty offences (defamation, minor theft, public misconduct).

items.title: ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024: India Crowned World Champions Defeating South Africa
items.summary: The Indian Men's Cricket Team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024, defeating South Africa by 7 runs in the final at Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, Barbados, ending an 11-year ICC trophy drought.
items.crux: India became the first team in T20 World Cup history to win the tournament undefeated, claiming their second T20 World Cup title (first won in 2007 under MS Dhoni).
takeaways: Virat Kohli named Player of the Match in the Final (76 off 59 balls).
Jasprit Bumrah named Player of the Tournament (15 wickets at an economy rate of 4.17).
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli formally announced their retirement from T20 International cricket following the victory.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Champions: India (2nd title); Runners-up: South Africa; Player of Tournament: Jasprit Bumrah.

mcq.question: Who was awarded the 'Player of the Tournament' award at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
options: Virat Kohli
Rohit Sharma
Jasprit Bumrah
Hardik Pandya
mcq.explanation: Jasprit Bumrah was named Player of the Tournament for taking 15 wickets with a phenomenal economy rate of 4.17.

items.title: Indian Sovereign Bonds Included in JP Morgan GBI-EM & Bloomberg Global Indices
items.summary: Indian Government Bonds (G-Secs) under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) were formally included in the flagship JP Morgan Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets (GBI-EM) Global Diversified index with a 10% maximum weight.
items.crux: Index inclusion is estimated to trigger foreign portfolio inflows of $25–30 billion, broadening the investor base for central government debt and lowering domestic borrowing yields.
takeaways: India's weight scaled up by 1% per month until reaching the maximum cap of 10% in the index.
Only eligible dated securities issued under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) with no foreign investment caps qualify.
Bloomberg Emerging Market Local Currency Government Index also announced inclusion of Indian FAR bonds.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) & JP Morgan
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Max weight: 10% in GBI-EM; Estimated inflows: $25–30 Billion; Security category: FAR G-Secs.

mcq.question: Which category of Indian Government Securities was made eligible for inclusion in global bond indices like JP Morgan GBI-EM?
options: State Development Loans (SDLs)
Treasury Bills (91-day T-Bills)
G-Secs under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR)
Special Oil Bonds
mcq.explanation: Only dated government securities issued under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR), introduced by RBI in 2020 with zero FPI limits, are eligible for index inclusion.

items.title: Telecommunications Act 2023 Replaces 138-Year-Old Indian Telegraph Act 1885
items.summary: Key provisions of the Telecommunications Act 2023 came into effect, replacing the colonial Indian Telegraph Act 1885 and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act 1933 with a modern legal framework for spectrum management and national security.
items.crux: The Act introduces administrative allocation of satellite communication spectrum (Satcom), replaces licensing with an authorization regime, and establishes the Digital Bharat Nidhi replacing the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF).
takeaways: Allows administrative (non-auction) assignment of spectrum for satellite broadband, maritime, and public safety services (First Schedule).
Digital Bharat Nidhi broadens USOF scope to support telecom research, pilot projects, and underserved rural areas.
Provides statutory right-of-way (RoW) framework ensuring non-discriminatory access for telecom infrastructure rollout.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Replaces: Indian Telegraph Act 1885; USOF renamed to: Digital Bharat Nidhi; Satcom spectrum: Administrative route.

mcq.question: Under the Telecommunications Act 2023, the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) has been renamed and repurposed as:
options: BharatNet Development Fund
Digital Bharat Nidhi
National Telecom Infrastructure Corpus
Telecom Innovation Trust
mcq.explanation: Section 24 of the Telecommunications Act 2023 establishes the 'Digital Bharat Nidhi' as the modernized successor to the USOF.

items.title: Deep Ocean Mission: Samudrayaan 'MATSYA 6000' Manned Submersible Tested
items.summary: The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, completed shallow water wet tests of the indigenous manned submersible 'MATSYA 6000' under the flagship Deep Ocean Mission.
items.crux: MATSYA 6000 is engineered to carry three humans to a depth of 6,000 meters in the Indian Ocean to survey polymetallic nodules, hydrothermal sulfides, and deep-sea biodiversity using a titanium alloy personnel sphere.
takeaways: Deep Ocean Mission has a 5-year outlay of ₹4,077 crore to harness living and non-living marine resources.
International Seabed Authority (ISA) has allocated 75,000 sq km in the Central Indian Ocean Basin to India for polymetallic nodule exploration.
Only five countries (US, Russia, France, Japan, and China) possess human submersibles capable of diving to 6,000 meters.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) & NIOT Chennai
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Vehicle: MATSYA 6000; Depth: 6,000 m; Personnel: 3 humans; Hull material: 80mm Titanium alloy sphere.

mcq.question: The indigenous manned deep-ocean submersible being developed by NIOT under India's Deep Ocean Mission is named:
options: VARUNA 5000
MATSYA 6000
SAGARIKA 3000
SAMUDRA 7000
mcq.explanation: MATSYA 6000 is the manned submersible vehicle designed to take 3 scientists to a depth of 6,000 meters in the ocean.

items.title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY 2.0): Target to Construct 3 Crore Additional Homes
items.summary: In its first cabinet decision, the Union Government approved financial assistance for the construction of 3 crore additional houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)—2 crore houses under PMAY-Gramin and 1 crore under PMAY-Urban 2.0.
items.crux: Addresses the housing needs of poor, lower-middle, and middle-class families with enhanced basic amenities including toilet, LPG connection, tap water, and electricity under convergence with other welfare missions.
takeaways: PMAY-U 2.0 introduces an Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS) for home loans up to ₹35 lakh for EWS and LIG categories.
All houses require mandatory ownership or co-ownership in the name of the female head of the family.
Constructed using disaster-resilient green technologies with geo-tagging at each stage of construction.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total houses: 3 Crore (2 Cr Rural + 1 Cr Urban); Gender empowerment: Mandatory female co-ownership.

mcq.question: Under the expanded PMAY 2.0 guidelines approved in 2024, what is the total number of additional houses planned to be constructed?
options: 1 Crore
2 Crore
3 Crore
5 Crore
mcq.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved financial assistance to construct 3 crore additional houses (2 crore under PMAY-Gramin and 1 crore under PMAY-Urban).

items.title: RBI Launches PRAVAAH Portal, Retail Direct Mobile App & FINNET 2.0 System
items.summary: RBI launched three major digital initiatives: the PRAVAAH portal for centralized regulatory approvals, the RBI Retail Direct Mobile App for retail G-Sec investing, and the FINNET 2.0 system.
items.crux: PRAVAAH (Platform for Regulatory Application, VAlidation And AutHorisation) streamlines regulatory clearances across 60 application forms, while Retail Direct Mobile App democratizes individual participation in G-Secs.
takeaways: Retail Direct Scheme allows individual investors to directly open a Gilt Securities Account (Retail Direct Gilt Account) with RBI without intermediary broker fees.
Supports investment in Government of India Dated Securities, Treasury Bills (T-Bills), State Development Loans (SDLs), and Sovereign Gold Bonds.
PRAVAAH enhances ease of doing business for banks, NBFCs, and payment system operators.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: PRAVAAH: Platform for Regulatory Application, VAlidation And AutHorisation; Retail Direct: zero fee G-Sec access.

mcq.question: What is the primary objective of the 'PRAVAAH' portal launched by the Reserve Bank of India?
options: Conducting interbank foreign exchange swaps.
Centralized online processing of regulatory permissions and statutory approvals.
Resolving delayed payments to MSME vendors.
Monitoring cyber security incidents across commercial banks.
mcq.explanation: PRAVAAH is a secure web-based portal designed for individuals and entities to apply online for regulatory licenses and approvals from the RBI.

items.title: Sengol Installed in New Parliament: Chola Dynasty Symbol of Righteous Governance
items.summary: The historic golden sceptre 'Sengol' was consecrated and placed adjacent to the Lok Sabha Speaker's chair in the New Parliament Building, reviving an ancient Tamil tradition of ethical rule and power transition.
items.crux: Originating from the Imperial Chola dynasty, the Sengol (derived from the Tamil word 'Semmai' meaning righteousness) represents the transfer of power and the ruler's solemn duty to govern justly under 'Dharma'.
takeaways: Crafted in 1947 by Vummidi Bangaru Chetty jewelers on the guidance of C. Rajagopalachari and Thiruvavaduthurai Adheenam mutt.
Handed to first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on August 14, 1947, as a sacred symbol of independence from British rule.
Topped by a carved recumbent Nandi (the bull of Shiva), symbolizing unyielding justice, steadfast truth, and duty.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Lok Sabha Secretariat & Ministry of Culture
prelims_pointers.location: Lok Sabha Chamber, New Parliament House, New Delhi
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Dynasty: Chola; Symbol at crest: Nandi (righteousness); Tamil origin: Semmai; Mutt: Thiruvavaduthurai Adheenam.

mcq.question: The crest of the golden sceptre 'Sengol', installed in the Lok Sabha chamber, features which carved sacred motif symbolizing justice?
options: Ashoka Lion Capital
Recumbent Nandi (the sacred bull)
Peacock with open feathers
Dharma Chakra with 24 spokes
mcq.explanation: The Sengol is surmounted by a hand-carved Nandi, representing righteousness, steadfastness, and unbiased justice.

items.title: PM Gati Shakti & National Logistics Policy (NLP): Logistics Performance Index Jumps to 38th
items.summary: India's ranking in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI) improved by 6 places to 38th among 139 countries, driven by the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP).
items.crux: PM Gati Shakti provides a GIS-based digital platform integrating infrastructure plans of 16 ministries to eliminate bureaucratic silos, optimize multi-modal freight connectivity, and reduce logistics cost to single-digit GDP percentages.
takeaways: National Logistics Policy (NLP) sets targets to reduce logistics cost in India to comparable global benchmarks by 2030.
ULIP integrates 34 logistics systems of 8 ministries through open APIs for end-to-end cargo visibility.
Enables National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity across highways, railways, ports, airports, and inland waterways.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: National Logistics Policy 2022 & PM Gati Shakti NMP
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: LPI Rank: 38th / 139 (World Bank); Gati Shakti: 16 Central Ministries on BISAG-N GIS platform.

mcq.question: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI), India's rank improved to which position?
options: 44th
38th
32nd
28th
mcq.explanation: India jumped six places to rank 38th out of 139 countries in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI).

items.title: PM-eBus Sewa Scheme: Deployment of 10,000 Electric Buses Across 169 Urban Centers
items.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs signed contracts under the 'PM-eBus Sewa' scheme to roll out 10,000 electric buses on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model across 169 cities lacking organized public bus transport.
items.crux: With an estimated cost of ₹57,613 crore (Central support ₹20,000 crore), the scheme supports city bus operations for 10 years, promoting electric mobility and green power charging infrastructure.
takeaways: Priority given to cities with a population between 3 lakh and 40 lakh, including capital cities of Union Territories and North-Eastern States.
City authorities contract private bus operators on Gross Cost Contract (GCC) basis while receiving operational subsidies per kilometer from Centre.
Reduces urban tailpipe emissions, diesel import bills, and congestion in Tier-2 and Tier-3 urban areas.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Buses: 10,000 e-buses; Total cost: ₹57,613 Crore; Model: PPP with Gross Cost Contract (GCC).

mcq.question: What business model is adopted under the PM-eBus Sewa scheme for operating 10,000 electric buses in designated cities?
options: Direct municipal government ownership and operation
Public-Private Partnership (PPP) on Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model
Fully privatized fare-metering without state subsidies
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) grant operations
mcq.explanation: Under PM-eBus Sewa, city bus operations are run through a PPP framework on a Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model with central operational support.

items.title: Project Cheetah Phase 2: Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary Prepared as Second African Cheetah Habitat
items.summary: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) completed predator-proof fencing and prey-base augmentations at Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh, preparing it to receive the next batch of African cheetahs under Project Cheetah.
items.crux: Gandhi Sagar serves as the second home to disperse cheetahs from Kuno National Park to prevent territorial overcrowding, establishing a viable metapopulation across the Chambal river landscape.
takeaways: Cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952; reintroduced in September 2022 from Namibia and South Africa.
Gandhi Sagar sanctuary is located in Mandsaur and Neemuch districts of MP on the Chambal river basin.
Over 17 cubs have been born on Indian soil at Kuno National Park since reintroduction.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) & MP Forest Department
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India
prelims_pointers.location: Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary (Mandsaur/Neemuch, MP) & Kuno NP (Sheopur, MP)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Cheetah declared extinct in India: 1952; Reintroduced: 2022; New second site: Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary.

mcq.question: Which wildlife sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh has been readied as the second habitat to receive reintroduced African cheetahs after Kuno National Park?
options: Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary
Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary
Ratapani Wildlife Sanctuary
Bagdara Wildlife Sanctuary
mcq.explanation: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary in Mandsaur and Neemuch districts of MP was prepared as the second home for cheetahs under Project Cheetah.

items.title: Bharat 6G Vision Document & 'Bharat 6G Alliance' Launched by DoT
items.summary: The Department of Telecommunications unveiled the 'Bharat 6G Vision' document and formally launched the 'Bharat 6G Alliance' (B6GA) to position India as a leading global supplier of intellectual property, products, and standards in sixth-generation telecommunications.
items.crux: Operates under the guiding principles of Affordability, Sustainability, and Ubiquity, aiming for commercial 6G deployment by 2030 and securing at least 10% of global standard patents.
takeaways: 6G is expected to deliver ultra-low latency (<1 millisecond) and speeds up to 1 Terabit per second (Tbps), 100 times faster than 5G.
International Telecommunication Union (ITU) officially approved the 6G Framework (IMT-2030), adopting key inputs submitted by India.
Supported by an accelerated R&D funding corpus under the Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Target year: 2030; ITU designation for 6G: IMT-2030; Core themes: Affordability, Sustainability, Ubiquity.

mcq.question: What is the official terminology adopted by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) for sixth-generation (6G) wireless technology systems?
options: IMT-Advanced
NextGen Wireless 2030
mcq.explanation: The ITU formally approved the framework for 6G under the technical designation 'IMT-2030'.

items.title: D Gukesh Wins FIDE Candidates 2024 to Become Youngest World Title Challenger in History
items.summary: 17-year-old Grandmaster Dommaraju Gukesh won the FIDE Candidates Tournament 2024 in Toronto, Canada, becoming the youngest player in chess history to win the Candidates and earn the right to challenge the reigning World Champion.
items.crux: Gukesh broke Garry Kasparov's 40-year-old record (set at age 20 in 1984), scoring 9 out of 14 points against an elite field including Hikaru Nakamura, Fabiano Caruana, and Ian Nepomniachtchi to challenge Ding Liren.
takeaways: Became only the second Indian after Viswanathan Anand to qualify for a World Chess Championship match.
Koneru Humpy and Vaishali Rameshbabu finished joint second in the Women's Candidates tournament.
Crowned World Champion match venue later hosted in Singapore in late 2024.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Age: 17; Record: Youngest Candidates winner (surpassed Kasparov); Score: 9/14.

mcq.question: Who became the youngest challenger in World Chess Championship history by winning the FIDE Candidates Tournament 2024 in Toronto?
options: Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa
Arjun Erigaisi
Dommaraju Gukesh
Nodirbek Abdusattorov
mcq.explanation: 17-year-old D Gukesh won the Candidates tournament with 9/14 points, breaking Garry Kasparov's longstanding record.

items.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme: Financial Aid & Skill Toolkits for 18 Traditional Artisan Trades
items.summary: The Central Sector 'PM Vishwakarma Scheme' achieved over 2 crore applicant registrations, providing holistic handholding to traditional artisans and craftspeople working with their hands and traditional tools across 18 family-based trades.
items.crux: Offers recognition through PM Vishwakarma Certificate & ID card, skill upgradation stipend (₹500/day), toolkit incentive of ₹15,000, and collateral-free enterprise development loans up to ₹3 lakh at a concessional 5% interest rate.
takeaways: Fully funded by Central Government with an initial outlay of ₹13,000 crore for FY24 to FY28.
Credit support provided in two tranches: Tranche 1 up to ₹1 lakh (18 months) and Tranche 2 up to ₹2 lakh (30 months).
Covers 18 trades including carpenters (Suthar), blacksmiths (Lohar), goldsmiths (Sonar), potters (Kumhaar), weavers, and boat builders.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of MSME, Ministry of Skill Development, and Department of Financial Services
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Outlay: ₹13,000 Crore; Trades covered: 18; Loan: Up to ₹3 Lakh at 5% interest; Toolkit grant: ₹15,000.

mcq.question: Under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme, what is the concessional interest rate charged to beneficiary artisans for collateral-free credit?
mcq.explanation: The scheme offers collateral-free loans up to ₹3 lakh at a concessional interest rate of 5%, with interest subvention provided by the Central Government.

items.title: National Quantum Mission (NQM): Hub-and-Spoke Thematic Research Ecosystem
items.summary: The Department of Science and Technology (DST) approved guidelines for four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) under the ₹6,003 crore National Quantum Mission (NQM) to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50-1000 physical qubits.
items.crux: NQM focuses on four core verticals: Quantum Computing, Quantum Communication, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, and Quantum Materials & Devices, positioning India among the top 6 global quantum leaders.
takeaways: Aims to achieve satellite-based secure quantum communications over a ground distance of 2,000 km.
Develops quantum key distribution (QKD) over terrestrial fiber networks and multi-node quantum networks.
Targets development of high-sensitivity magnetometers, atomic clocks, and superconducting quantum chips.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Outlay: ₹6,003 Crore (2023-2031); 4 T-Hubs: Computing, Communication, Sensing, Materials.

mcq.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) established under India's National Quantum Mission?
options: Quantum Computing
Quantum Communication
Quantum Sensing and Metrology
Quantum Space Propulsion
mcq.explanation: The four verticals of NQM are: Quantum Computing, Quantum Communication, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, and Quantum Materials & Devices.

items.title: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023: Data Protection Board & Compliance Rules
items.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) progressed implementation rules for the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023, operationalizing the Data Protection Board of India and cross-border data transfer protocols.
items.crux: DPDP Act grants citizens ('Data Principals') rights to access, correction, and erasure of personal data, imposing stringent fiduciary obligations on organizations ('Data Fiduciaries') with penalties up to ₹250 crore for significant data breaches.
takeaways: Applies to processing of digital personal data within India and processing outside India if offering goods or services to Data Principals in India.
Establishment of the Data Protection Board of India as an independent digital-first adjudicatory body.
Mandates verifiable parental consent for processing data of children (below 18 years).

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Data Protection Board of India & MeitY
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Max penalty: ₹250 Crore per breach; Child defined as under 18; Negative list approach for cross-border data transfer.

mcq.question: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, what is the maximum financial penalty that can be imposed for failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach?
options: ₹50 Crore
₹100 Crore
₹250 Crore
₹500 Crore
mcq.explanation: Section 33 and Schedule of the DPDP Act 2023 prescribe penalties up to ₹250 Crore for failing to prevent a significant personal data breach.

items.title: Project Tiger Completes 50 Years: NTCA Census Records 3,682 Wild Tigers in India
items.summary: Celebrating 50 years of Project Tiger (launched in 1973), the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) released the Status of Tigers report, revealing India's tiger population reached a minimum of 3,167 and an estimated upper mean of 3,682 wild tigers.
items.crux: India is now home to approximately 75% of the world's wild tiger population, growing at an annual rate of 6.1%, with Central India and the Shivalik Hills-Gangetic plains recording significant population expansions.
takeaways: Madhya Pradesh retained its status as the 'Tiger State of India' with 785 tigers, followed by Karnataka (563) and Uttarakhand (560).
Corbett Tiger Reserve has the highest tiger density with 260 tigers inside the reserve.
55 tiger reserves currently notified across India, with Dholpur-Karauli (Rajasthan) and Veerangana Durgavati (MP) as recent additions.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) & Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total tigers: 3,682; Top State: Madhya Pradesh (785); Top Reserve: Corbett (260); Global share: ~75%.

mcq.question: According to the 5th cycle All India Tiger Estimation report, which Indian state holds the highest population of wild tigers?
options: Karnataka
Uttarakhand
Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra
mcq.explanation: Madhya Pradesh recorded 785 tigers, making it the state with the highest tiger population in India.

items.title: Supreme Court Recognizes Fundamental Right to be Free from Adverse Effects of Climate Change
items.summary: In M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India, a 3-judge Supreme Court bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud formally recognized an explicit fundamental right to be free from the adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution.
items.crux: While balancing the conservation of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB) with the development of solar power transmission corridors in Rajasthan and Gujarat, the Court held that the right to life is incomplete without climate stability.
takeaways: The Court held that the right to health and a clean environment under Article 21 intrinsically includes freedom from catastrophic climate disruption.
Article 14 (Equality) applies because marginalized and vulnerable communities disproportionately suffer from climate-induced droughts and floods.
Appointed an expert committee to assess where underground vs overhead transmission lines can coexist with GIB bird flight diverters.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Articles 21, 14, 48A, and 51A(g) of the Constitution of India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Case: M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India; Species: Great Indian Bustard (GIB - Critically Endangered, IUCN Red List).

mcq.question: In which landmark 2024 judgment did the Supreme Court explicitly recognize the 'right to be free from the adverse effects of climate change' as part of Articles 14 and 21?
options: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Taj Trapezium case)
M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India (Great Indian Bustard case)
Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India
mcq.explanation: In M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court ruled that citizens have a fundamental right under Articles 14 and 21 to be free from adverse climate change impacts.

items.title: NexCAR19: India's First Indigenous CAR-T Cell Gene Therapy Approved for Cancer
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu dedicated to the nation 'NexCAR19' (Actalycabtagene autoleucel), India's first indigenously developed CAR-T (Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell) therapy, developed collaboratively by IIT Bombay and ImmunoACT.
items.crux: NexCAR19 genetically reprograms the patient's own T-cells to identify and eliminate cancer cells, targeting B-cell lymphomas and leukemia at one-tenth of global commercial costs.
takeaways: Approved by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) for relapsed/refractory B-cell malignancies.
First humanized CAR-T cell therapy designed to reduce neurotoxicity and cytokine release syndrome.
Supported by the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) National Biopharma Mission.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: IIT Bombay, ImmunoACT & Tata Memorial Hospital
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 & CDSCO approval
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Therapy name: NexCAR19; Target: CD19 protein on cancerous B-cells; Cost: ~₹30–40 lakh vs ₹4 crore overseas.

mcq.question: What is the mechanism of action of 'NexCAR19', India's first indigenously developed CAR-T cell therapy?
options: It uses monoclonal antibodies to block angiogenesis in tumors.
It genetically re-engineers patient's own T-cells with a chimeric receptor to destroy CD19-expressing cancer cells.
It deploys radioactive isotopes directly into bone marrow.
It suppresses cellular division via mRNA transcription inhibition.
mcq.explanation: CAR-T cell therapy extracts the patient's own T-cells, genetically modifies them with a Chimeric Antigen Receptor to target the CD19 antigen on cancer cells, and re-infuses them.

items.title: Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023: $2 Trillion Export Target & Internationalization of Rupee
items.summary: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry rolled out initiatives under Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023, shifting from an incentive-based to an automated remission-based regime targeting $2 Trillion in exports by 2030.
items.crux: FTP 2023 has no fixed sunset date, promoting Indian Rupee invoicing in foreign trade through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) and identifying 39 Towns of Export Excellence (TEE).
takeaways: Four Pillars: Incentive to Remission, Export promotion through collaboration (Districts as Export Hubs), Ease of Doing Business, and Emerging Areas (E-Commerce).
E-commerce export cap per consignment via courier increased from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
Designated 4 new Towns of Export Excellence (Faridabad, Mirzapur, Moradabad, Varanasi) taking total TEE count to 43.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) & Commerce Ministry
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Export target: $2 Trillion by 2030 ($1T merchandise + $1T services); Policy duration: Dynamic (no sunset date).

mcq.question: What is the targeted total export value (merchandise and services combined) set under India's Foreign Trade Policy 2023 for the year 2030?
options: $1 Trillion
$1.5 Trillion
$2 Trillion
$3 Trillion
mcq.explanation: FTP 2023 sets an ambitious target of achieving $2 Trillion in overall exports ($1 Trillion goods and $1 Trillion services) by 2030.

items.title: SEBI Launches T+0 Rolling Settlement Beta Cycle for Indian Equity Cash Markets
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) commenced the beta version of optional same-day (T+0) rolling settlement for a select basket of 25 liquid scrips alongside the existing T+1 cycle.
items.crux: T+0 enables instantaneous receipt of funds and securities in client demat accounts on the transaction day itself, eliminating counterparty settlement risk.
takeaways: India became the second country after China to operate a widespread T+1 settlement cycle in 2023, and now pioneers optional T+0.
Full instantaneous trade settlement (Instantaneous Settlement) is planned as the ultimate phase.
Improves liquidity, releases blocked broker margins faster, and protects retail investors from settlement delays.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: T+0 Beta covers 25 scrips; trades executed up to 1:30 PM; optional for retail and institutional traders.

mcq.question: Under the T+0 settlement framework introduced by SEBI, trade settlement occurs:
options: Within 24 hours of trade execution.
On the trade day itself (same-day).
At the end of the trading week.
Instantly on continuous blockchain ledger.
mcq.explanation: T+0 settlement delivers shares to the buyer's demat and funds to the seller's bank account on the exact date of trade execution.

items.title: Jal Jeevan Mission: Reaches Milestone of 75%+ Rural Households with Tap Water Connections
items.summary: On World Water Day, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation announced that over 75% of rural households in India (over 14.5 crore families) have been provided with functional household tap water connections under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM).
items.crux: JJM aims to provide 55 liters per capita per day (lpcd) of potable drinking water to every rural household ('Har Ghar Jal') through functional household tap connections (FHTC) by 2024.
takeaways: Nine States and Union Territories have achieved 100% 'Har Ghar Jal' certification: Goa, Telangana, Haryana, Gujarat, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Puducherry, D&D/D&NH, and A&N Islands.
Water Quality Management Information System (WQMIS) integrates field test kits and NABL-accredited labs for potability surveillance.
Implemented under community ownership with Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSC) / Pani Samitis.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: National Jal Jeevan Mission launched 15 August 2019
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Supply norm: 55 liters per capita per day; First 100% Har Ghar Jal state: Goa; First certified district: Burhanpur (MP).

mcq.question: What is the prescribed minimum quantity of safe potable drinking water provided per person per day under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
options: 40 liters per capita per day
55 liters per capita per day
70 liters per capita per day
100 liters per capita per day
mcq.explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide 55 liters of water per person per day to every rural household through Functional Household Tap Connections.

items.title: Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA): 24 Nations Join Clean Energy Compact
items.summary: The Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA), initiated by India alongside Brazil and the United States on the sidelines of the New Delhi G20 Summit, expanded to 24 member nations and 12 international organizations to accelerate sustainable biofuel trade.
items.crux: GBA aims to facilitate technology transfers, develop harmonized international biofuel standards, and promote blending mandates (e.g. India's E20 target of 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025-26).
takeaways: Co-founded by India, Brazil, and the US, who collectively account for 85% of global ethanol production and 81% of consumption.
International organizations supporting GBA include the International Energy Agency (IEA), International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), and World Bank.
Promotes sustainable 2G (second-generation) ethanol from agricultural biomass (paddy straw, bagasse) reducing stubble burning.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) & GBA Secretariat
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Lead founders: India, US, Brazil; India's ethanol blending target: E20 by 2025-26.

mcq.question: Which three nations are the founding core members of the Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA)?
options: India, Germany, and France
India, United States, and Brazil
India, Russia, and Saudi Arabia
India, Australia, and Japan
mcq.explanation: India, the United States, and Brazil—the world's largest biofuel producers—co-founded the Global Biofuels Alliance.

items.title: One Nation One Election: Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee Submits Report
items.summary: The High-Level Committee (HLC) on Simultaneous Elections chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind submitted its unanimous 18,626-page report recommending synchronized two-step elections across Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and local bodies.
items.crux: Recommends introducing Article 82A via constitutional amendment to notify an 'Appointed Date', synchronizing Lok Sabha and Assembly tenures, followed by local body elections within 100 days.
takeaways: Step 1: Synchronize Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly elections (does not require ratification by States).
Step 2: Synchronize Municipalities and Panchayats elections within 100 days of General Elections (requires ratification by at least half of the States).
Proposes single Common Electoral Roll and Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) across all three tiers of governance.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections & Ministry of Law and Justice
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chairman: Ram Nath Kovind; Committee members included Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap.

mcq.question: According to the Ram Nath Kovind Committee recommendations, synchronizing elections to Municipalities and Panchayats with general elections requires:
options: Simple majority in Parliament without State consent.
Constitutional amendment ratified by at least half of the State Legislatures.
An executive notification under Representation of the People Act.
Supreme Court approval under Article 142.
mcq.explanation: Amending local government election timelines affects State subjects (Entries 5 & 6, List II) and therefore requires ratification by not less than half the States.

items.source: PIB / Ministry of Law and Justice

items.title: Agni-5 with MIRV (Mission Divyastra): Multiple Nuclear Warhead Technology Tested
items.summary: DRDO successfully conducted the maiden flight test of the indigenously developed Agni-5 missile equipped with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology under the codename 'Mission Divyastra'.
items.crux: MIRV technology allows a single intercontinental ballistic missile to carry multiple nuclear warheads, each capable of being programmed to strike separate targets hundreds of kilometers apart, defeating ballistic missile defence shields.
takeaways: India joined an elite league of nations with proven MIRV capability (US, Russia, China, France, and UK).
Equipped with indigenous avionics systems and high-accuracy sensor packages ensuring pinpoint terminal accuracy.
Agni-5 is a three-stage solid-fuel missile with a strike range exceeding 5,000 kilometers, capable of road-mobile canisterized launch.

prelims_pointers.location: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha coast
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Mission Divyastra; Range: >5,000 km; Propulsion: 3-stage solid; MIRV: Multiple warheads on independent vectors.

mcq.question: What is the defining capability of an ICBM equipped with MIRV technology as demonstrated in 'Mission Divyastra'?
options: It can refuel liquid propellant during supersonic flight.
A single missile carries multiple warheads that can strike independent targets across different geographic coordinates.
It can fly below radar horizon using scramjet air-breathing propulsion.
It can only be detected by ocean acoustic sonar.
mcq.explanation: MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) allows a single ballistic missile to deploy multiple warheads, each guided to hit separate designated targets.

items.title: India-EFTA Trade & Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA): $100B Investment Pact
items.summary: India signed the landmark Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)—comprising Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein—securing a binding commitment of $100 billion foreign direct investment over 15 years.
items.crux: TEPA is India's first modern FTA featuring a binding legal commitment on investment promotion and 1 million direct job creations in exchange for tariff concessions on 95%+ of EFTA industrial exports.
takeaways: EFTA countries gain zero or reduced tariff access for Swiss watches, Norwegian salmon, precision machinery, and chocolates.
India excluded sensitive agricultural products (dairy, soya, coal, sensitive agricultural lines) to protect domestic farmers.
First trade agreement incorporating dedicated chapters on Sustainable Development and Environmental Obligations.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Commerce and Industry & EFTA Secretariat
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Article XXIV of GATT 1994 (Regional Trade Agreements)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: EFTA 4 nations: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein (Non-EU European bloc); $100B FDI over 15 years.

mcq.question: Which four countries comprise the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) that signed the TEPA pact with India in 2024?
options: Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Norway
Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein
Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Netherlands
United Kingdom, Norway, Switzerland, Ireland
mcq.explanation: EFTA was established in 1960 and currently consists of Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.

items.title: IndiaAI Mission: ₹10,372 Crore Allocation for Sovereign 10,000 GPU Computing
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the comprehensive IndiaAI Mission with a financial outlay of ₹10,372 crore to establish a sovereign compute ecosystem with over 10,000 GPUs for AI startups and research.
items.crux: The mission democratizes AI compute access under a Public-Private Partnership model, develops foundational AI models for Indian languages, and establishes the IndiaAI Datasets Platform.
takeaways: IndiaAI Compute Capacity: Subsidized access to supercomputing infrastructure for startups, researchers, and academia.
IndiaAI Innovation Centre: Developing indigenous multimodal Foundation Models trained on Indic datasets.
IndiaAI FutureSkills: Establishing Data and AI Labs across Tier-2 and Tier-3 academic institutions.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Outlay: ₹10,372 Crore over 5 years; Target: 10,000+ AI GPUs compute capacity.

mcq.question: What is the targeted GPU computing capacity planned to be established under the approved IndiaAI Mission?
options: 2,500 GPUs
5,000 GPUs
10,000 or more GPUs
50,000 GPUs
mcq.explanation: The IndiaAI Mission has an approved budget of ₹10,372 crore to build an AI compute infrastructure of 10,000 or more graphics processing units (GPUs).

items.title: High-Yield GI Tags 2024: Majuli Masks, Cuttack Silver Filigree & Risa Textile Inscribed
items.summary: The Geographical Indications Registry granted GI certificates to prominent traditional crafts, including Cuttack Rupa Tarakasi (Odisha), Majuli Masks and Manuscript Paintings (Assam), and Risa Textile (Tripura).
items.crux: GI status confers legal protection against unauthorized imitation under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act 1999, certifying quality and geographic uniqueness.
takeaways: Cuttack Rupa Tarakasi: Ancient delicate silver filigree craft dating back over 500 years with fine silver wire ornamentation.
Majuli Masks (Mukha Shilpa): Bamboo, clay, and cowdung devotional masks made by Neo-Vaishnavite Satras for Bhaona folk theater.
Risa: Customary handwoven indigenous female chest wrapper worn by indigenous Tripuri tribal communities.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Geographical Indications Registry, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: GI validity: 10 years (renewable); First Indian GI tag: Darjeeling Tea (2004-05).

mcq.question: Which historic handicraft from Odisha, known for its delicate fine-wire silver filigree work, was awarded the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2024?
options: Pipili Applique Craft
Cuttack Rupa Tarakasi
Raghurajpur Pattachitra
Dhokra Bell Metal
mcq.explanation: Cuttack's famous Rupa Tarakasi (silver filigree) was granted the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in March 2024.

items.title: Chief Election Commissioner and other ECs Act 2023: New Appointment Procedure
items.summary: Parliament enacted the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, establishing a statutory selection committee to replace the ad-hoc executive appointment process.
items.crux: Under the new law, CEC and ECs are appointed by the President upon recommendation of a 3-member Selection Committee consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), a Union Cabinet Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) / Leader of the single largest opposition party in Lok Sabha.
takeaways: Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel of five candidates for the Selection Committee.
Conditions of service, salary, and allowances aligned with that of a Supreme Court Judge.
Replaced the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Election Commission of India (ECI) & Law Ministry
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Selection Committee: PM + Cabinet Minister + LoP in Lok Sabha; Tenure: 6 years or 65 years of age.

mcq.question: Under the CEC and other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service) Act 2023, who chairs the Selection Committee?
options: Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister of India
Speaker of Lok Sabha
Union Minister of Law and Justice
mcq.explanation: The Selection Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister of India, with a designated Union Cabinet Minister and the Leader of Opposition as members.

items.source: Ministry of Law and Justice / PIB

items.title: India Semiconductor Mission: Dholera Commercial Fab & Packaging Units Underway
items.summary: Under the ₹76,000 crore India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), construction commenced on India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility in Dholera, Gujarat by Tata Electronics in partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC).
items.crux: The ₹91,000 crore Dholera mega-fab will produce 28nm, 50nm, and 90nm nodes for automotive, power electronics, and computing, complemented by OSAT/ATMP units in Sanand and Morigaon.
takeaways: Central Government provides 50% fiscal support on a pari-passu basis for fab and packaging units.
Tata OSAT plant in Jagiroad, Morigaon (Assam) represents the first major semiconductor investment in Northeast India.
Critical for de-risking global chip supply chains and securing sovereign electronics hardware capabilities.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) & Digital India Corporation (MeitY)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Outlay: ₹76,000 Crore; Tech partner: PSMC Taiwan; First commercial fab: Dholera, Gujarat.

mcq.question: India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication plant approved under the India Semiconductor Mission is being established at:
options: Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu
Dholera, Gujarat
NOIDA, Uttar Pradesh
Bengaluru, Karnataka
mcq.explanation: Tata Electronics is constructing the first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility at Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR), Gujarat.

items.title: Critical Minerals Auction: Strategic Lithium, Graphite & Rare Earth Blocks Tranches
items.summary: The Ministry of Mines launched multiple tranches of auction for critical and strategic mineral blocks, including Lithium (Salal-Haimana block in Reasi, J&K, and Katghora in Chhattisgarh), Titanium, Nickel, Chromium, and Rare Earth Elements (REE).
items.crux: Enacted following amendments to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, empowering the Union government to auction 24 critical minerals essential for EV batteries and defence.
takeaways: MMDR Amendment Act 2023 introduced an Exploration Licence (EL) to encourage private sector reconnaissance.
De-listed six atomic minerals including Lithium and Beryllium from atomic list to allow private commercial mining.
Secures raw material resilience for India's National Electric Mobility and net-zero clean energy goals.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Mines & Geological Survey of India (GSI)
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: MMDR Amendment Act 2023 & Part D of First Schedule
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Lithium reserves: 5.9 million tonnes G3 inferred resources in Reasi, J&K.

mcq.question: Which legislative enactment in 2023 enabled the central government to auction 24 critical and strategic minerals directly to private miners?
options: National Green Tribunal Amendment Act
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023
Atomic Energy (Special Provisions) Act
Mineral Concession Rules 1960 repeal
mcq.explanation: The MMDR Amendment Act 2023 introduced Part D to the First Schedule specifying 24 critical and strategic minerals for central auctioning.

items.title: International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Headquarters Formally Founded in India
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) with its headquarters in India, alongside a one-time budgetary grant of ₹150 crore for five years.
items.crux: IBCA is a multi-country, multi-agency coalition of 97 big-cat range countries dedicated to the conservation of seven major big cats: Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah, Jaguar, and Puma.
takeaways: Launched during the 50th anniversary commemoration of Project Tiger in Mysuru, Karnataka.
India is the only country in the world to host five of the seven big cats in the wild (Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah).
Governance framework includes a General Assembly of member states and an elected Council headed by a President.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: International treaty-based organisation headquarters in India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 7 Big Cats: Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah, Jaguar, Puma; Initial grant: ₹150 Crore.

mcq.question: Which two big cats included in the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) are NOT naturally found in the wild in India?
options: Jaguar and Puma
Snow Leopard and Cheetah
Leopard and Tiger
Cheetah and Lion
mcq.explanation: Jaguars (native to the Americas) and Pumas (native to the Americas) are not found in the wild in India.

items.title: Gaganyaan Mission: Prime Minister Reveals 4 IAF Astronaut Designates & CE-20 Cryogenic Engine Human-Rated
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the names of the four Indian Air Force test pilots selected as astronaut-designates for India's maiden human spaceflight mission, Gaganyaan, while ISRO successfully human-rated the CE-20 cryogenic engine.
items.crux: Gaganyaan aims to demonstrate human spaceflight capability by launching a 3-member crew to an orbit of 400 km for a 3-day mission and returning them safely to Earth with a splashdown in Indian sea waters.
takeaways: Four Astronauts: Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair, Group Captain Ajit Krishnan, Group Captain Angad Prathap, and Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla.
Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla selected as prime pilot for the Indo-US joint Axiom-4 (Ax-4) mission to the International Space Station (ISS).
Launch vehicle is the Human-Rated LVM3 (HLVM3) equipped with Crew Escape System (CES) tested in TV-D1 flight.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Vehicle: HLVM3; Orbit: 400 km Low Earth Orbit; Crew: 3 astronauts for 3 days; First test humanoid: Vyommitra.

mcq.question: Which Indian Air Force officer was selected as the prime pilot astronaut for the Axiom-4 (Ax-4) joint space mission to the International Space Station?
options: Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair
Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla
Group Captain Ajit Krishnan
Group Captain Angad Prathap
