mcq.explanation: Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla was chosen as the prime mission pilot for the Axiom-4 mission to the ISS.

items.title: Supreme Court Unanimously Strikes Down Electoral Bonds Scheme as Unconstitutional
items.summary: A 5-judge Constitution Bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud unanimously invalidated the 2018 Electoral Bonds Scheme, ruling that anonymous corporate political funding violates the voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a).
items.crux: The Supreme Court struck down amendments to the Companies Act, Representation of the People Act, and Income Tax Act, ordering SBI to disclose all donor and recipient bond data to ECI for public display.
takeaways: Ruled that voter's right to information is essential to exercise freedom of speech and expression and to evaluate corporate influence on government policy.
Rejected the government's argument that confidentiality of political donors is necessary to curb black money (doctrine of proportionality failed).
Struck down amendment to Section 182 of Companies Act that had removed the 7.5% cap on corporate political donations.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Supreme Court of India & Election Commission of India (ECI)
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Constitution of India, Art 19(1)(a), Section 29C of RPA 1951
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Bench: 5 judges (CJI D.Y. Chandrachud, Sanjiv Khanna, B.R. Gavai, J.B. Pardiwala, Manoj Misra). Unanimous verdict.

mcq.question: In striking down the Electoral Bonds scheme, the Supreme Court held that the scheme violated which fundamental right of voters?
options: Right to equality under Article 14 only
Right to information under Article 19(1)(a)
Right to privacy under Article 21 only
Freedom of conscience under Article 25
mcq.explanation: The 5-judge bench held that non-disclosure of political funding violates the voters' right to information anchored in Article 19(1)(a).

items.source: Supreme Court of India / The Hindu

items.title: Santiniketan & Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
items.summary: UNESCO inscribed Rabindranath Tagore's ashram school Santiniketan (West Bengal, 41st site) and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura in Karnataka, 42nd site) on the World Heritage List.
items.crux: Hoysala temples (12th-13th century) epitomize the stellate (star-shaped) ground plan, chloritic schist (soapstone) intricate friezes, and Vesara architectural synthesis under King Vishnuvardhana and Narasimha I.
takeaways: Three Hoysala temples: Chennakeshava Temple at Belur, Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu, and Keshava Temple at Somanathapura.
Santiniketan was founded in 1901 by Rabindranath Tagore based on ancient Indian Gurukul traditions and pan-Asian internationalism.
Features the famous signed sculptures of Hoysala master craftsmen like Dasoja, Chavana, and Mallitamma.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Hoysala sites: Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura; Material: Soapstone (Chloritic Schist); Plan: Stellate.

mcq.question: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas inscribed by UNESCO feature which distinctive architectural ground plan and building material?
options: Octagonal ground plan built entirely with red sandstone
Stellate (star-shaped) plan built with chloritic schist (soapstone)
Circular stupa plan built with unburnt mud bricks
Panchayatana plan built using granite monolithic blocks
mcq.explanation: Hoysala temple architecture is characterized by stellate (star-shaped) vimana platforms and the extensive use of soapstone (chloritic schist) for intricate miniature carving.

items.title: BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi: First Traditional Stone Temple in Middle East Inaugurated
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, marking the first traditional stone-carved Hindu temple in the Middle East region.
items.crux: Built on 27 acres of land gifted by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the temple features seven spires (shikhars) representing the seven emirates of the UAE, constructed without steel or ferrous metals.
takeaways: Constructed using pink sandstone from Rajasthan and Italian Carrara marble using ancient Nagara-style stone interlocking techniques.
Symbolizes mutual tolerance, communal harmony, and the vibrant Indian diaspora ties in West Asia.
Depicts value tales from Indian epics alongside traditional Arabic, Mayan, Aztec, and Egyptian civilizational fables.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha & UAE Ministry of Tolerance
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Architectural features: 7 spires (7 emirates), Nagara style, Pink sandstone from Rajasthan, No structural steel.

mcq.question: The BAPS Hindu Mandir inaugurated in Abu Dhabi features seven spires (shikhars). What do the seven spires symbolically represent?
options: The seven holy rivers of India (Sapta Sindhu)
The seven Emirates that constitute the UAE
The seven celestial sages (Saptarishi)
The seven continents of the world
mcq.explanation: The seven shikhars (spires) of the Abu Dhabi temple symbolize the unity of the seven emirates of the UAE.

items.title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Launched with ₹75,021 Crore Outlay for 1 Crore Solar Homes
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the 'PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana' with a total financial outlay of ₹75,021 crore, aimed at providing up to 300 units of free electricity every month to 1 crore households through rooftop solar installations.
items.crux: Provides central financial assistance (subsidy) up to ₹78,000 for 3 kW rooftop solar systems, integrated with low-interest collateral-free bank loans at around 7% interest through a National Portal.
takeaways: Subsidy structure: ₹30,000 for 1 kW system, ₹60,000 for 2 kW system, and ₹78,000 for 3 kW or higher systems.
Urban local bodies and Panchayats incentivized to develop 'Model Solar Villages' in every district.
Projected to save households ₹75,000 crore annually in electricity bills and reduce carbon emissions by 720 million tonnes.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Outlay: ₹75,021 Crore; Target: 1 Crore households; Free electricity: Up to 300 units/month; Max subsidy: ₹78,000.

mcq.question: Under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, what is the maximum central financial subsidy provided for a 3 kW or higher residential rooftop solar system?
mcq.explanation: The scheme provides a maximum subsidy of ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW capacity or higher.

items.title: Vadnagar Excavations: Continuous Human Settlement for 2,800 Years Confirmed by ASI
items.summary: A deep multidisciplinary excavation at Vadnagar in Mehsana district, Gujarat, led by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in collaboration with IIT Kharagpur, unearthed evidence of continuous human occupation dating back to 800 BCE.
items.crux: Challenges the notion of a 'Dark Age' between the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization and the Second Urbanization of the Gangetic Plains, proving unbroken cultural continuity through 7 distinct cultural periods.
takeaways: Seven cultural periods identified: Pre-Rampart (Mauryan/Pre-Mauryan), Indo-Greek, Indo-Scythian/Kshatrapa, Maitraka/Solanki, Sultanate, Mughal, and Gaekwad.
Uncovered Buddhist monastery ruins, amphitheater, Roman amphora pottery shards, and shell bangles proving trans-oceanic trade links.
Vadnagar was mentioned as 'Anartapura' in the Mahabharata and visited by Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang in the 7th century CE.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & IIT Kharagpur
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chronology: 800 BCE to modern era (2,800 years); 7 cultural strata; Visited by Hiuen Tsang (640 CE) who described 10 Buddhist monasteries.

mcq.question: Which Chinese Buddhist pilgrim visited the ancient town of Vadnagar (then Anandapura) in the 7th century CE and recorded the existence of Buddhist monasteries?
options: Fa-Hien
Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)
I-Tsing
Song Yun
mcq.explanation: Hiuen Tsang visited Vadnagar in 640 CE, writing that Anandapura was a major center with 10 Buddhist monasteries housing over 1,000 monks of the Sammitiya school.

items.title: Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs): RBI Auctions Tranches to Fund Climate Mitigation Projects
items.summary: The RBI, on behalf of the Government of India, issued Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) to mobilize resources for public sector projects aimed at reducing the carbon intensity of the economy.
items.crux: Proceeds from SGrBs are exclusively deployed in public expenditures related to renewable energy, clean transportation, water management, and energy efficiency under the Framework for Sovereign Green Bonds.
takeaways: Issued as dated government securities with tenors of 5 years, 10 years, and 30 years eligible for SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio).
Non-resident investors can invest in SGrBs under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).
A Green Finance Working Committee (GFWC) chaired by the Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) selects eligible green expenditure.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: SGrBs are SLR eligible; classified under FAR route; nuclear power and large hydro (>25MW) excluded.

mcq.question: Under the Framework for Sovereign Green Bonds issued by the Ministry of Finance, which of the following is EXCLUDED from eligible green expenditures?
options: Solar and wind power generation projects.
Dedicated freight corridors and metro rail projects.
Nuclear power generation and extraction of fossil fuels.
Afforestation and biodiversity conservation programs.
mcq.explanation: The framework explicitly excludes projects involving nuclear power, fossil fuel extraction, and large hydro projects >25 MW.

items.title: Maratha Military Landscapes of India Nominated for UNESCO World Heritage Recognition
items.summary: India nominated the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' as its official submission for the UNESCO World Heritage List cycle 2024–2025, comprising 12 strategic hill, coastal, and island forts developed under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
items.crux: The network exemplifies guerrilla warfare ('Ganimi Kava') landscape integration, utilizing Western Ghats cliff topography and Konkan naval fortresses between the 17th and 19th centuries.
takeaways: 11 forts in Maharashtra: Salher, Shivneri, Lohagad, Khanderi, Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Suvarnadurg, Panhala, Vijaydurg, and Sindhudurg.
1 fort in Tamil Nadu: Gingee Fort (dubbed the 'Troy of the East' by the British).
Integrates hill forts, coastal sea forts (Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg), and island citadens (Khanderi, Suvarnadurg).

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Government of Maharashtra
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: UNESCO Operational Guidelines for World Heritage
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total forts: 12 (11 in Maharashtra + 1 Gingee in Tamil Nadu); Era: 17th-19th Century CE.

mcq.question: Which fort located in Tamil Nadu is included among the 12 nominated sites of the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' for UNESCO World Heritage recognition?
options: Vellore Fort
Gingee Fort
Thanjavur Maratha Palace
Dindigul Fort
mcq.explanation: Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu is the sole non-Maharashtra fort included in the 12 nominated Maratha Military Landscapes.

items.title: Rohan Bopanna Becomes Oldest Grand Slam Champion and World No. 1 in Tennis History
items.summary: Rohan Bopanna won the Australian Open 2024 Men's Doubles title alongside Australian partner Matthew Ebden, becoming the oldest man in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam title and to reach ATP World No. 1 ranking at the age of 43.
items.crux: Bopanna defeated Italian duo Simone Bolelli and Andrea Vavassori in straight sets, surpassing Mike Bryan's previous record as the oldest Grand Slam doubles champion.
takeaways: Conferred the Padma Shri award in 2024 for extraordinary contributions to Indian tennis.
Became only the fourth Indian tennis player to achieve the ATP World No. 1 doubles ranking after Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, and Sania Mirza.
Won his first men's doubles Major after 61 Grand Slam appearances.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Age: 43 years, 329 days; Partner: Matthew Ebden (Australia); Rank: ATP World No. 1.

mcq.question: At age 43, Rohan Bopanna won the Men's Doubles title at the Australian Open 2024 partnering with:
options: Simone Bolelli
Matthew Ebden
Wesley Koolhof
Ivan Dodig
mcq.explanation: Rohan Bopanna partnered with Australian player Matthew Ebden to lift the Australian Open 2024 Men's Doubles title.

items.title: Vadnagar Archaeological Excavations: 2,800-Year Continuous Settlement Uncovered
items.summary: A collaborative excavation led by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and IIT Kharagpur uncovered evidence of continuous human settlement in Vadnagar, Gujarat dating back to 800 BCE.
items.crux: The findings challenge the narrative of a prolonged 'Dark Age' between the collapse of the Indus Valley Civilization and the emergence of the Early Historic second urbanization in the Gangetic plain.
takeaways: Reveals seven successive cultural stages: Pre-Rambha, Mauryan, Indo-Greek, Kshatrapa, Solanki/Chalukya, Sultanate, and Gaekwad-modern periods.
Vadnagar was historically known as Anartapura, Anandapura, and Chamatkarpur, visited by Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang in the 7th century CE.
Excavations revealed an ancient Buddhist monastery with stupas, terracotta artifacts, Roman amphora shards, and coin mints.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & IIT Kharagpur
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Settlement date: 800 BCE (Late Vedic / Iron Age); 7 cultural layers; Xuanzang noted 10 Buddhist monasteries here.

mcq.question: Which ancient town in Gujarat recently revealed evidence of continuous human habitation spanning 2,800 years across seven successive cultural periods?
options: Dholavira
Lothal
Vadnagar
Rangpur
mcq.explanation: Excavations at Vadnagar (Mehsana, Gujarat) proved continuous settlement from 800 BCE through the Mauryan, Solanki, and modern eras.

items.title: Governor's Assent to Bills: Supreme Court Clarifies Article 200 Timelines
items.summary: The Supreme Court delivered significant constitutional rulings in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor and Tamil Nadu matters, holding that Governors cannot withhold assent to state bills indefinitely and must act promptly.
items.crux: CJI-led bench held that if a Governor withholds assent under the first proviso to Article 200, the bill MUST be returned to the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible with a message, and if re-passed, the Governor has no option but to grant assent.
takeaways: The phrase 'as soon as possible' in the first proviso to Article 200 contains an inherent constitutional obligation to act with dispatch.
A Governor cannot defeat the legislative will of an elected legislature by pocket-vetoing a bill without returning it.
Clarified that the Governor is a symbolic constitutional head and must act on aid and advice of Council of Ministers except in discretionary areas.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Supreme Court of India & State Legislatures
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Articles 200, 201, and 163 of the Constitution of India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Art 200 gives 4 options to Governor: Assent, Withhold, Return for reconsideration, or Reserve for President (Art 201).

mcq.question: Under Article 200 of the Constitution, if a State Legislative Assembly re-passes a returned bill with or without amendments, the Governor:
options: Can withhold assent indefinitely.
Shall not withhold assent therefrom.
Must compulsorily refer the bill to the Supreme Court.
Can dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
mcq.explanation: Article 200 explicitly mandates that if a bill is passed again by the Legislature with or without amendment, 'the Governor shall not withhold assent therefrom'.

items.title: National Green Hydrogen Mission: SIGHT Program Tranches Awarded for 5 MMT Target
items.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) awarded letters of award under the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) program, supporting electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production under the ₹19,744 crore mission.
items.crux: Aims to build at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) per annum of green hydrogen production capacity by 2030, abating nearly 50 MMT of annual greenhouse gas emissions and saving ₹1 lakh crore in fossil fuel imports.
takeaways: Outlay of ₹19,744 crore: ₹17,490 crore for SIGHT program, ₹1,466 crore for pilot projects, and ₹400 crore for R&D.
Designated ports (Deendayal, Paradip, and VO Chidambaranar) are being developed as Green Hydrogen Hubs.
Notified green hydrogen standards requiring well-to-gate emissions not exceeding 2 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of H2.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: MNRE & Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI)
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: National Green Hydrogen Mission approved January 2023
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Mission outlay: ₹19,744 Crore; Target: 5 MMT Green H2 per annum by 2030; Associated RE addition: 125 GW.

mcq.question: What is the annual production target of Green Hydrogen set under the National Green Hydrogen Mission by 2030?
options: 1 Million Metric Tonne (MMT)
2.5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)
5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)
10 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)
mcq.explanation: The mission aims to develop green hydrogen production capacity of at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) per annum by 2030.

items.title: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC): Strategic Multimodal Connectivity
items.summary: India, US, Saudi Arabia, UAE, France, Germany, Italy, and EU advanced planning on the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), agreed on the sidelines of the New Delhi G20 Summit.
items.crux: IMEC comprises two distinct corridors: the Eastern Corridor connecting India to the Arabian Gulf and the Northern Corridor connecting the Gulf to Europe via rail and shipping routes.
takeaways: Reduces transit time between India and Europe by 40% and logistics costs by 30% compared to the Suez Canal route.
Includes clean hydrogen pipeline, high-speed digital data cables, and electricity grids alongside railway tracks.
Serves as a transparent, high-standard alternative to China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) under the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII).

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of External Affairs & Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII)
prelims_pointers.location: Mundra / JNPT Ports (India) to Fujairah / Jebel Ali (UAE), Haifa (Israel), Piraeus (Greece)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: IMEC MoU signatories: India, US, Saudi Arabia, UAE, France, Germany, Italy, EU.

mcq.question: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) consists of two segments: the Eastern corridor and the Northern corridor. What does the Northern corridor connect?
options: India to the Arabian Gulf
Arabian Gulf to Europe
Central Asia to Europe
Red Sea to Mediterranean Sea directly
mcq.explanation: The Eastern Corridor connects India to the Gulf, while the Northern Corridor connects the Arabian Gulf to European ports via rail and maritime shipping.

items.title: Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP): First Delta Rankings for 500 Blocks Announced
items.summary: NITI Aayog published the inaugural Delta Rankings for the Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP), recognizing Tiriyani Block of Kumuram Bheem Asifabad district (Telangana) with the 1st rank and Kaushambi block (Uttar Pradesh) with the 2nd rank.
items.crux: Building on the success of the Aspirational Districts Programme, ABP focuses on fast-tracking development across 500 historically lagging blocks in 329 districts across 40 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
takeaways: KPIs categorized into 5 themes: Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources, Basic Infrastructure, and Social Development.
Launched the 'Chintan Shivir' and 'Sankalp Saptaah' nationwide governance convergence campaigns.
Employs competitive federalism and peer learning to empower grassroot block administration.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Top block: Tiriyani (Telangana); 2nd: Kaushambi (UP); Coverage: 500 blocks.

mcq.question: Which administrative block achieved the top position in NITI Aayog's first-ever Delta Rankings under the Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP)?
options: Kaushambi Block, Uttar Pradesh
Tiriyani Block, Telangana
Aripal Block, Jammu and Kashmir
Nandurbar Block, Maharashtra
mcq.explanation: Tiriyani block of Kumuram Bheem Asifabad district in Telangana secured the top rank in NITI Aayog's first ABP Delta Rankings.

items.title: Swachh Survekshan Awards: Indore and Surat Crowned Joint Cleanest Cities in India
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards, where Indore (for the 7th consecutive year) and Surat were declared the joint cleanest cities in India in the category of cities with more than 1 lakh population.
items.crux: Navi Mumbai was ranked the third cleanest city, while Maharashtra bagged the award for the best-performing State in sanitation, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
takeaways: Conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U).
Saswad in Maharashtra was ranked the cleanest city among urban local bodies with population below 1 lakh.
Varanasi and Prayagraj emerged as the cleanest Ganga towns.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
prelims_pointers.location: New Delhi / Indore, Surat, Navi Mumbai
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Cleanest cities (>1 lakh): Indore & Surat (Joint 1st); Best state: Maharashtra; Cleanest Ganga town: Varanasi.

mcq.question: Which two cities were jointly awarded the title of 'Cleanest City' (population > 1 Lakh) at the Swachh Survekshan Awards?
options: Indore and Bhopal
Indore and Surat
Surat and Navi Mumbai
Chandigarh and Mysuru
mcq.explanation: Indore and Surat shared the top honor as joint cleanest cities in the more than 1 lakh population category.

items.title: UNESCO Inscribes 'Garba of Gujarat' on Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage
items.summary: UNESCO officially inscribed 'Garba of Gujarat' onto the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (ICH), making it the 15th intangible cultural heritage element from India on the list.
items.crux: Garba is a devotional ritualistic dance performed during the nine-day Hindu festival of Navratri, celebrating the divine feminine force (Shakti) symbolized by a perforated earthen pot (Garbha Deep) with an oil lamp inside.
takeaways: Celebrates social inclusivity, gender equality, and communal bonding across all sections of society.
Earlier Indian entries on UNESCO ICH list include Durga Puja in Kolkata (2021), Kumbh Mela (2017), Yoga (2016), and Vedic chanting (2008).
The decision was announced during the 18th session of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the ICH held in Kasane, Botswana.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Culture & Sangeet Natak Akademi
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 15th Indian element on UNESCO ICH list; Performed during Sharad Navratri around Garbha Deep.

mcq.question: Which of the following elements is the 15th Intangible Cultural Heritage from India to be inscribed by UNESCO?
options: Chhau dance
Durga Puja of Kolkata
Garba of Gujarat
Kumbh Mela
mcq.explanation: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed as the 15th element from India on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in December 2023.

items.title: Garba of Gujarat Inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List
items.summary: UNESCO inscribed 'Garba of Gujarat' on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity under the 2003 Convention, during its 18th session in Kasane, Botswana.
items.crux: Garba is a devotional ritualistic dance performed during the nine-day Hindu festival of Navratri, centered around an earthen lamp (Garbha Deep) or an idol of Goddess Durga/Amba, symbolizing life and feminine divinity.
takeaways: Garba became the 15th intangible cultural heritage element from India on UNESCO's list.
Earlier inscriptions include Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Vedic Chanting, Durga Puja of Kolkata (2021), and Chhau Dance.
Fosters social inclusion, community cohesion, and transmission of devotional poetry across generations.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Sangeet Natak Akademi & Ministry of Culture
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: UNESCO 2003 Convention for Safeguarding Intangible Cultural Heritage
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 15th Indian element on UNESCO ICH list; Associated with: Navratri & feminine energy (Shakti).

mcq.question: The traditional dance form 'Garba of Gujarat', inscribed by UNESCO on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list, is traditionally performed around:
options: A sacred fire altar (Yajna kunda)
A perforated earthenware pot with an oil lamp inside (Garbha Deep)
A ceremonial harvest sickle
A bronze idol of Nataraja
mcq.explanation: Garba derives from the Sanskrit word 'Garbha' (womb) and is performed in circular patterns around a perforated earthen pot containing a lamp (Garbha Deep).

items.title: 16th Finance Commission Formally Constituted: Dr. Arvind Panagariya Appointed Chairman
items.summary: The President of India constituted the 16th Finance Commission with former NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Dr. Arvind Panagariya as Chairman, tasked with recommending the tax devolution formula between Union and States for the 5-year period starting April 1, 2026.
items.crux: The Commission operates under Article 280, mandated to review vertical tax sharing, grants-in-aid principles under Article 275, and financing of Disaster Management initiatives under Disaster Management Act 2005.
takeaways: Constitutional body constituted every 5 years under Article 280 of the Constitution.
15th Finance Commission (chaired by N.K. Singh) had recommended 41% vertical devolution to States (adjusted from 42% after reorganization of J&K into UTs).
Report must be submitted by October 31, 2025, covering the award period 2026-2031.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chairman: Dr. Arvind Panagariya; Secretary: Ritvik Ranjanam Pandey; Award tenure: 2026-2031.

mcq.question: Under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and how many other members?
options: 3 other members
4 other members
5 other members
6 other members
mcq.explanation: Article 280(1) specifies that the Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.

items.title: Aditya-L1 Spacecraft Placed in Sun-Earth Lagrange Point L1 Halo Orbit
items.summary: ISRO successfully injected India's first solar observatory mission, Aditya-L1, into a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrangian Point L1, approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
items.crux: From the L1 vantage point, Aditya-L1 continuously observes the Sun without any occultation or eclipses, monitoring solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and space weather using 7 indigenous payloads.
takeaways: Launched aboard PSLV-C57 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
Primary payload is the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru.
SUIT (Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope) captured unprecedented full-disk UV images of the solar photosphere and chromosphere.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Department of Space, Government of India
prelims_pointers.location: Lagrange Point 1 (L1), 1.5 million km from Earth
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 7 payloads: 4 remote sensing (VELC, SUIT, ASPEX, PAPA) + 3 in-situ (MAG, SoLEXS, HEL1OS).

mcq.question: What is the primary advantage of placing the Aditya-L1 solar observatory in a halo orbit around Lagrange Point 1 (L1)?
options: It enables the spacecraft to land on the solar surface.
It provides continuous, uninterrupted view of the Sun without occultation or eclipses.
It eliminates all solar radiation pressure on the spacecraft.
It allows the satellite to re-enter Earth's atmosphere periodically for maintenance.
mcq.explanation: Lagrange Point 1 offers an uninterrupted view of the Sun without any occultation or eclipse from the Earth, ensuring continuous solar monitoring.

items.title: 37th National Games Goa: Maharashtra Topped Medal Tally with Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy
items.summary: The 37th National Games concluded in Goa with Maharashtra finishing atop the medal standings with 228 medals (80 Gold, 69 Silver, 79 Bronze), winning the prestigious Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy for the first time since 1994.
items.crux: Services Sports Control Board (SSCB) finished second with 66 Gold medals, while Haryana finished third with 62 Gold medals in the multi-sport event featuring 43 disciplines.
takeaways: Official Mascot of the 37th National Games was 'Moga' (an Indian bison / Gaur representing love in Konkani).
Traditional martial arts Gatka, Kalaripayattu, Yogasana, and Mallakhamb featured prominently.
38th edition of the National Games awarded to Uttarakhand.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) & Sports Authority of Goa
prelims_pointers.location: Goa (five cities: Panaji, Margao, Mapusa, Ponda, Vasco)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Champions: Maharashtra (228 medals); Trophy: Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy; Mascot: Moga (Gaur).

mcq.question: Which state contingent lifted the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy by topping the overall medal tally at the 37th National Games held in Goa?
options: Services (SSCB)
Haryana
Maharashtra
Kerala
mcq.explanation: Maharashtra topped the medal tally with 80 gold and 228 overall medals to claim the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy.

items.title: COP28 UAE Consensus & COP29 Baku Summit: Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels
items.summary: The UNFCCC COP28 in Dubai adopted the historic 'UAE Consensus', calling on all nations to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems to achieve net zero by 2050, followed by the COP29 summit in Baku focusing on the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance.
items.crux: COP28 formally operationalized the Loss and Damage Fund hosted by the World Bank, and set global targets to triple renewable energy capacity and double energy efficiency rates by 2030.
takeaways: COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, was dubbed the 'Finance COP' to negotiate a new financial target replacing the previous $100 billion annual climate pledge.
India advocated for climate justice, differentiation under Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), and affordable technology transfer.
India launched the Green Credits Initiative (GCI) on the sidelines of COP28 to incentivize voluntary environmental positive actions.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: COP28: UAE Consensus, Loss & Damage Fund; COP29: Baku, Azerbaijan (NCQG Climate Finance); India's Net Zero target: 2070.

mcq.question: The primary agenda and focus of the COP29 climate summit held in Baku, Azerbaijan was negotiating the:
options: Global Methane Pledge enforcement.
New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance.
Universal carbon border adjustment mechanism.
Global plastic ban treaty.
mcq.explanation: COP29 in Baku was dubbed the 'Finance COP', focused on establishing the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) to replace the $100 billion/year climate finance target.

items.title: XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) Launched by ISRO PSLV-C58
items.summary: ISRO kicked off the year by launching XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) onboard PSLV-C58 into a 650 km Low Earth Orbit, making India only the second country in the world after the US (NASA's IXPE) to operate a dedicated space-based X-ray polarimetry mission.
items.crux: XPoSat studies the polarization of intense astronomical X-ray sources like black hole binaries, neutron stars, active galactic nuclei, and pulsar wind nebulae in the medium energy band (8-30 keV).
takeaways: Carries two scientific payloads: POLIX (Polarimeter Instrument in X-rays) developed by Raman Research Institute (RRI), and XSPECT (X-ray Spectroscopy and Timing) by URSC.
PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM-3) utilized the spent fourth stage (PS4) as an orbital platform for 10 microgravity payloads.
Complements NASA's IXPE mission by measuring polarization in a higher energy X-ray band.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Department of Space, Government of India
prelims_pointers.location: Low Earth Orbit (650 km altitude, 6-degree inclination)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Launch vehicle: PSLV-C58; Payloads: POLIX (8-30 keV) and XSPECT (0.8-15 keV).

mcq.question: Which institute developed the primary scientific payload 'POLIX' (Polarimeter Instrument in X-rays) for ISRO's XPoSat mission?
options: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)
Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru
Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad
Indian Institute of Science (IISc)
mcq.explanation: POLIX was designed and built by the Raman Research Institute (RRI) in Bengaluru in collaboration with the U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC).
